source_text: Universal human rights frameworks, including New Zealand's obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, assert bodily integrity as non-negotiable, overriding claims when data shows victim suffering—such as lifelong sexual dysfunction and mental health disorders—outweighs purported communal benefits like enhanced social cohesion. [26]
